source: {fn} is a function, so it needs brackets: {fn}(*) or {fn}(column).
note: Fires on `no such column: count`, which is what SQLite says about a bare `COUNT` — so the sentence has to undo that reading before a beginner goes looking through the table for a column named count.

source: {token} is not a column in {table}. Check the table card for the real names.
text: {token}은 {table}의 열이 아닙니다. 테이블 카드에서 실제 이름을 확인하십시오.
note: The same fault with the table named, which is only possible when the query reads one. Worth its own key: "in this table" is a sentence about a table it never names, and the schema panel is showing four of them.
group diagnosis: What SQLite said, in the player's terms.

source: From {token} onward, SQL cannot read the query. Something before it is unfinished.
text: {token}부터는 SQL이 질의를 읽지 못한다. 그 앞부분이 완성되지 않았다.
note: group diagnosis: What SQLite said, in the player's terms.

source: {token} is not a function SQL knows.
note: group diagnosis: What SQLite said, in the player's terms.

source: {token} counts a group, so the query needs a GROUP BY to say which rows go together.
text: {token}은 그룹을 집계하므로, 어떤 행을 묶을지 지정하는 GROUP BY가 질의에 필요하다.
note: group diagnosis: What SQLite said, in the player's terms.

source: {token} appears in both tables, so SQL cannot tell which you mean. Put the table in front of it: table.{token}.
text: {token}이 두 테이블 모두에 있어서 SQL이 어느 쪽인지 구분하지 못합니다. 그 앞에 테이블을 붙이십시오: table.{token}.
note: group diagnosis: What SQLite said, in the player's terms.

source: {token} cannot be read by SQL. Most often an opening quote lacks a closing one.
text: {token}은 SQL이 읽지 못한다. 대부분 여는 따옴표에 닫는 따옴표가 빠진 탓이다.
note: group diagnosis: What SQLite said, in the player's terms.

source: The query stops before it finishes. The last clause is still waiting for something: a column, a value, or a closing bracket.
text: 질의가 끝나기 전에 끊겼다. 마지막 절이 열, 값 또는 닫는 괄호를 아직 기다리고 있다.
note: group diagnosis: What SQLite said, in the player's terms.

source: SQL cannot read this query. Look for a missing quote, comma or bracket, or a clause that stops halfway.
text: SQL이 이 질의를 읽지 못한다. 빠진 따옴표, 쉼표, 괄호가 있는지, 혹은 중간에 끊긴 절이 있는지 확인하십시오.
note: Said when SQLite's own words cannot be trusted: its parser quotes whatever it was holding when it gave up, which is not always something the player wrote. An error describing code you did not write is worse than none.
Appended to the sentence above it, so it opens with a space and every language's version has to as well.

source: '{value}' matched nothing. Perhaps you meant '{real}'. Capitals count inside quotes.
text: '{value}'와 일치하는 항목이 없다. 혹시 '{real}'을 뜻하셨습니까? 따옴표 안에서는 대소문자를 구분한다.
note: The hardest failure in the game: a query that compiled, ran, and found nothing, because `'criminal'` is not `'Criminal'` to SQLite and no error is raised. Only ever offered with a spelling the table really holds, so the quotes around both values are part of the sentence.

source: The console only reads. A query starts with SELECT. Nothing here can change the evidence.
text: 흰색 패널은 읽기만 한다. 질의는 SELECT로 시작한다. 이곳의 어떤 것도 증거를 변경하지 못한다.
note: The console reads, never writes. A player who typed DELETE or UPDATE is not making a mistake so much as asking for something the game does not do, and the sentence says so without scolding.

source: One query at a time. Nothing ran: remove the ";" in the middle, or run each query on its own.
text: 질의는 한 번에 하나씩입니다. 아무것도 실행되지 않았습니다: 중간의 “;”을 지우거나 각 질의를 따로 실행하십시오.
note: Two queries in the box, or one cut in two by a stray `;`. Nothing was run. It used to say `readOnly`, which told a player whose query began with SELECT that a query begins with SELECT. The error strip prints plain text, so the semicolon is quoted the way the language quotes, never in a code span: a backtick would be printed as one.

source: More than 1,000,000 rows. Each table after FROM multiplies the rows by its own count. Link the tables with JOIN … ON, or add a WHERE.
text: 결과가 1,000,000행을 넘는다. FROM 뒤의 테이블마다 행 수가 곱해진다. JOIN … ON으로 테이블을 연결하거나 WHERE 절을 추가하십시오.
note: A result too large to hold: every table listed in FROM multiplies the rows by its own count, and five copies of a 52-row table is 380 million. `sqlEngine` stops at a million and throws a marker; this is what the player reads.

source: {table} is sealed. Clear checkpoint {number}, {title}, and it is yours.
note: A table the case holds but the player has not earned. SQLite calls it "no such table", which is indistinguishable from a typo, and the schema panel is listing the name by which the player found it. `{number}` is the checkpoint that opens it and `{title}` is that checkpoint's own title.

source: {table} is sealed. You have not requisitioned it yet.
text: {table}은 봉인되어 있다. 아직 열람을 요청하지 않았습니다.
note: group diagnosis: What SQLite said, in the player's terms.

source: This bracket closes one that was never opened.
text: 이 괄호는 열린 적 없는 괄호를 닫고 있다.

source: This bracket is never closed. Every ( needs a ).
text: 이 괄호는 닫히지 않았다. 모든 “(”에는 “)”가 필요하다.

source: This text never closes. A value in quotes needs one at each end: 'Fire'.
text: 이 문자열은 닫히지 않았다. 따옴표로 감싼 값은 양 끝에 하나씩 있어야 한다: 'Fire'.

source: The semicolon ends the query. Everything after it is a second query, and the console runs one at a time.
text: 세미콜론은 질의를 끝낸다. 그 뒤에 오는 것은 모두 두 번째 질의이며, 콘솔은 한 번에 하나씩만 실행한다.

source: {keyword} and {rest} need a space between them. As one word it reads as a name, and there is nothing by that name.
text: {keyword}와 {rest} 사이에 공백이 필요하다. 한 단어로 붙여 쓰면 이름으로 인식되며, 그런 이름은 존재하지 않는다.
note: Two halves of one word the player typed without a space — `SELECTcity`.

source: A space is missing between {left} and {right}. SQLite reads it anyway and answers, so nothing looks wrong.
text: {left}와 {right} 사이에 공백이 빠졌다. SQLite는 그대로 읽고 결과를 내놓으므로 겉보기에는 문제가 없어 보인다.
note: A closing quote run straight into the next word — `'2026-03-02'AND`. SQLite accepts it and answers, which is why this one is worth a sentence: the player is not told the query failed, they are handed rows.

source: 2 commas in a row. There is nothing between them.
text: 쉼표 2개가 연달아 붙어 있다. 둘 사이에 아무것도 없다.

source: A comma with nothing after it. A list separates its items. It does not end with a separator.
text: 뒤에 아무것도 없는 쉼표다. 목록은 항목 사이를 구분할 뿐이며, 구분 기호로 끝나지 않는다.

source: {clause} belongs before {after}, and here it comes after. The order is fixed: SELECT, FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY, LIMIT.
text: 여기서 {clause}은 {after} 뒤에 나오지만, 그 앞에 와야 한다. 순서는 고정되어 있다: SELECT, FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY, LIMIT.
note: `{clause}` is a SQL keyword — WHERE, GROUP BY — and the list after it is the order itself, so neither is translated.

source: There is nothing between those quotes, so nothing can match. Put the value inside them.
text: 따옴표 사이에 아무것도 없어서 어떤 것도 일치하지 않는다. 따옴표 안에 값을 넣으십시오.
note: Two quotes with nothing between them. It compiles, it runs and it returns nothing, so the desk said "no rows matched" and the player read that as an answer about the data. Fourteen Russian sessions submitted one on the same checkpoint: the identifiers are typed in Latin and the values are Cyrillic, so a filter costs a keyboard layout switch in the middle of the line, and a switch that does not ta…

source: Nothing is ever equal to NULL, not even NULL. The test is always false. Say IS NULL instead.
text: 어떤 것도 NULL과 같지 않으며, NULL 자신도 마찬가지다. 그 비교는 항상 거짓이다. 대신 IS NULL을 쓰십시오.

source: BETWEEN takes its 2 ends joined by AND, with no brackets and no comma. Write {fix}.
text: BETWEEN은 괄호나 쉼표 없이 AND로 양 끝 값 2개를 연결한다. {fix}와 같이 작성하십시오.
note: `BETWEEN ('17:31', '17:38')`, the two ends written as a list. `{fix}` is the same query rebuilt from the player's own two values, `BETWEEN '17:31' AND '17:38'`, and is SQL: never translated.

source: There is no column called {token}. Did you mean {near}? If {token} is a value, it needs quotes: '{token}'.
text: {token}이라는 열은 없다. {near}을 뜻하셨습니까? {token}이 값이라면 따옴표가 필요하다: '{token}'.
note: Two forms of the same fault: with a column close enough to suggest, and without. The suggestion is only offered when it can be proved.

source: {token} has no quotes, so SQL reads it as a column name. A text value needs them: '{token}'.
text: {token}에 따옴표가 없어서 SQL이 이를 열 이름으로 읽는다. 텍스트 값에는 따옴표가 필요하다: '{token}'.

source: Without quotes, SQL reads {token} as a subtraction and compares with {result}. A date needs quotes. Did you mean '{token}'?
text: 따옴표가 없어서 SQL이 {token}을 뺄셈으로 읽고 {result}와 비교한다. 날짜에는 따옴표가 필요하다. '{token}'을 뜻하셨습니까?
note: A date or a time typed with no quotes. `{token}` is what the player typed, `{result}` what SQL computed from it: the subtraction is the whole explanation, so it is printed rather than described.

source: Without quotes, SQL cannot read the colon in {token}. A time needs quotes. Did you mean '{token}'?
text: 따옴표가 없어서 SQL이 {token}의 콜론을 읽지 못한다. 시각에는 따옴표가 필요하다. '{token}'을 뜻하셨습니까?

source: IN wants its list in brackets: IN ('one', 'two').
text: IN은 목록을 괄호로 감싸야 한다: IN ('one', 'two').

source: LIKE with no % has to match the whole value. Put % where the rest of the text may be: '%fire%'.
text: %가 없는 LIKE는 값 전체와 일치해야 한다. 나머지 텍스트가 올 수 있는 자리에 %를 넣으십시오: '%fire%'.

source: {token} on its own is not a test. Name the column again: {clause} column = {token}.
text: {token}만으로는 조건식이 되지 않는다. 열 이름을 다시 지정하십시오: {clause} column = {token}.
note: `{clause}` is WHERE or HAVING, and `column` in the example is the word the player should replace — a placeholder, not a column of any table.

source: Double quotes mean a column name, and there is no column called {inner}. Text values take single quotes: '{inner}'.
text: 큰따옴표는 열 이름을 뜻하지만, {inner}이라는 열은 없다. 텍스트 값에는 작은따옴표를 쓰십시오: '{inner}'.

source: A comma is missing before {token}. Without one, SQL reads it as a nickname for {prev} and returns a single column.
text: {token} 앞에 쉼표가 빠졌다. 쉼표가 없으면 SQL이 이를 {prev}의 별칭으로 읽어 하나의 열만 반환한다.
note: The commonest fault in the game, and the reason `nickname` is the word: an alias is what SQL calls it, and a beginner does not know the word yet.

source: A comma is missing before {token}. A name and a function cannot sit side by side. SQL stops at the bracket and refuses the whole query.
text: {token} 앞에 쉼표가 빠졌다. 이름과 함수는 나란히 올 수 없다. SQL은 괄호에서 멈추고 질의 전체를 거부한다.

source: A comma is missing before {token}, and there is no column called {token}. Did you mean {prev}, {near}?
text: {token} 앞에 쉼표가 빠졌으며, {token}이라는 열은 없다. {prev}, {near}을 뜻하셨습니까?
note: The missing comma with a misspelling on top of it, which is why it names three words: what was typed, what it was typed after, and the column it is one keystroke from. Without the comma the query runs and returns one column, so nothing else in the game will mention it.

source: WHERE chooses the rows, and {fn} counts the rows WHERE chose, so there is nothing there yet. Filter a total in HAVING, after the GROUP BY.
text: WHERE는 행을 고르고 {fn}은 WHERE가 고른 행을 집계하므로, 아직 그 자리에는 아무것도 없다. 집계 결과는 GROUP BY 뒤의 HAVING에서 거르십시오.
note: WHERE and HAVING are keywords and stay as they are. `{fn}` arrives upper-cased, the way the player has to type it.

source: {alias} is the name given in the SELECT, and WHERE is read first, so the name does not exist yet. Write the column out again here, or filter it in HAVING.
text: {alias}은 SELECT에서 지정한 이름인데, WHERE가 먼저 처리되므로 아직 그 이름이 존재하지 않는다. 여기에 열을 다시 적거나 HAVING에서 거르십시오.

source: {token} is a column of {other}, and this query only reads {table}. Requisition {other} and join it, or read the column from there.
text: {token}은 {other}의 열이며, 이 질의는 {table}만 읽는다. {other}을 요청하여 조인하거나, 해당 테이블에서 열을 읽으십시오.
note: `{table}` is what the FROM reads, `{other}` the table that has the column. Both are identifiers the player types.

source: 2 tables with nothing between them. {token} is being read as a nickname for {prev}. A JOIN needs the word JOIN and an ON.
text: 테이블 2개 사이에 아무것도 없다. {token}이 {prev}의 별칭으로 읽히고 있다. JOIN에는 JOIN이라는 단어와 ON이 필요하다.

source: Counting collapses every row into one, so only one {column} can come back, and SQL picks it at random. Add GROUP BY {column} to count per {column}.
text: 집계하면 모든 행이 하나로 합쳐지므로 {column}은 하나만 반환되며, SQL은 이를 무작위로 선택한다. {column}별로 집계하려면 GROUP BY {column}을 추가하십시오.

source: {column} is not in the GROUP BY, so each group shows whichever {column} SQL happened to read last. Group by it too, or leave it out.
text: {column}이 GROUP BY에 없으므로, 각 그룹은 SQL이 우연히 마지막으로 읽은 {column}을 표시한다. 이 열도 그룹화하거나 목록에서 빼십시오.

source: HAVING filters groups, and without a GROUP BY there is only one group. To filter rows, use WHERE.
text: HAVING은 그룹을 거르고, GROUP BY가 없으면 그룹은 하나뿐이다. 행을 거르려면 WHERE를 쓰십시오.

source: There is no table to read from here. Add FROM and the table name.
text: 여기서 읽을 테이블이 없다. FROM과 테이블 이름을 추가하십시오.

source: {table} is already in the FROM, so this joins it to itself. Join the other table: FROM {other} JOIN {table} ON …
text: {table}이 이미 FROM에 있으므로 자기 자신과 조인된다. 다른 테이블을 조인하십시오: FROM {other} JOIN {table} ON …
note: The same table on both sides of a JOIN, with no nickname to tell them apart. `{table}` is what the player typed; `{other}` the case's other table. Schema names, never translated.

source: {table} is already in the FROM, so this joins it to itself. Join the other table instead.
text: {table}이 이미 FROM에 있으므로 자기 자신과 조인된다. 대신 다른 테이블을 조인하십시오.

source: This JOIN has no matching columns, so it pairs every row with every row. Add ON table_a.column = table_b.column.
text: 이 JOIN은 일치시킬 열이 없어 모든 행을 서로 짝짓는다. ON table_a.column = table_b.column을 추가하십시오.

source: LIMIT takes the first rows, and with no ORDER BY it is SQL's choice which those are. Sort first to take the biggest, or the earliest.
text: LIMIT은 첫 행들을 가져오는데, ORDER BY가 없으면 어떤 행을 가져올지는 SQL 마음대로 결정된다. 가장 큰 값이나 가장 이른 값을 가져오려면 먼저 정렬하십시오.
